items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: In fact Don and I are playing there Friday night at this club right on Chippewa.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. There was a lot of places that really had top-notch, world-class musicians you know. And it was healthier in town. There was a lot of local things happening you know, and much healthier than it is now, although it’s picking up again in Buffalo. On the same street we mentioned, Chippewa, it’s like a rejuvenation. All the college people have discovered that area, and they’re all coming in and digging the music and hanging out and whatever they do you know. But it’s just coming back. In fact Don and I are…

He does all right. We’ve heard a lot of different stories about how musicians actually learned the craft of jazz. Some of them that were born in the 20s mostly learned it on the road. Was this something that you guys — how did you learn your craft?
